tasks.name: Setup Project Structure and Dependencies
tasks.description: Create the complete directory structure according to shrimp-rules.md specifications and establish Python dependencies management. This task creates the foundation for all subsequent development phases by setting up the exact file organization required for the object-oriented architecture.
tasks.notes: This establishes the foundation for all other tasks. Directory structure must match shrimp-rules.md exactly to maintain architectural compliance.

relatedFiles.description: Python dependencies file with typer and requests
Package initialization and domain exceptions definition

tasks.implementationGuide:
1. Create src/ directory with subdirectories: auth/, models/, repositories/, exceptions/
2. Add __init__.py files to make packages importable
3. Create requirements.txt with exact dependencies: typer>=0.9.0, requests>=2.31.0
4. Ensure directory structure matches: src/auth/auth_provider.py, src/models/client.py, src/models/invoice.py, src/repositories/repository.py, src/exceptions/__init__.py
5. Validate structure matches shrimp-rules.md specifications exactly
tasks.verificationCriteria: Directory structure exactly matches shrimp-rules.md specification. All __init__.py files exist and are importable. requirements.txt contains correct dependencies. Python can import all package modules without errors.
tasks.analysisResult: Phase 1 establishes the foundational object-oriented architecture for TightBeam v2 Jobber data migration tool. This creates core infrastructure components including authentication, data models, repository layer, and error handling with strict dependency injection patterns. The implementation follows exact specifications from shrimp-rules.md and prepares for seamless integration with Phase 2 (JobberClient, EntityMapper), Phase 3 (MigrationCoordinator, CLI), and Phase 4 (testing and refinement). All classes must use constructor-based dependency injection, single responsibility principle, and built-in dict type instead of typing.Dict (UP035 rule compliance).
tasks.summary: Successfully created complete project structure with src/ directory containing auth/, models/, repositories/, and exceptions/ subdirectories. All __init__.py files exist and are importable. Requirements.txt contains correct dependencies (typer>=0.9.0, requests>=2.31.0). All package modules import without errors. Directory structure exactly matches shrimp-rules.md specifications. Foundation established for object-oriented architecture with proper dependency injection patterns.

tasks.name: Implement Domain-Specific Exception Classes
tasks.description: Create domain-specific exception classes for clear error boundaries and proper error handling throughout the application. These exceptions provide meaningful error context and support the single responsibility principle by isolating error handling concerns.
tasks.notes: These exceptions are used by all other components and must be implemented before AuthProvider and Repository classes.
tasks.implementationGuide:
1. Define ConfigurationError for authentication and environment issues
2. Define JobberApiError for API communication failures
3. Define MappingError for data transformation issues
4. Define RepositoryError for database operation failures
5. All exceptions inherit from base Exception class
6. Include descriptive docstrings explaining when each exception should be raised
7. Follow Python exception naming conventions (Error suffix)
tasks.verificationCriteria: All four exception classes (ConfigurationError, JobberApiError, MappingError, RepositoryError) are defined and importable. Each has appropriate docstring. All inherit from base Exception. Can be imported from src.exceptions module.
tasks.analysisResult: Phase 1 establishes the foundational object-oriented architecture for TightBeam v2 Jobber data migration tool. This creates core infrastructure components including authentication, data models, repository layer, and error handling with strict dependency injection patterns. The implementation follows exact specifications from shrimp-rules.md and prepares for seamless integration with Phase 2 (JobberClient, EntityMapper), Phase 3 (MigrationCoordinator, CLI), and Phase 4 (testing and refinement). All classes must use constructor-based dependency injection, single responsibility principle, and built-in dict type instead of typing.Dict (UP035 rule compliance).

tasks.name: Create Entity Model Dataclasses
tasks.description: Implement Client and Invoice dataclasses representing Jobber API entities with proper type hints and field definitions. These models serve as the core data structures for the entire application and must match Jobber GraphQL schema exactly.
tasks.notes: Must use built-in dict type instead of typing.Dict (UP035 rule). Fields must match exact Jobber API schema for seamless data mapping in later phases.

relatedFiles.description: Client dataclass with Jobber API fields
Invoice dataclass with Jobber API fields

tasks.implementationGuide:
1. Create Client dataclass in src/models/client.py with fields: id (str), first_name (str), last_name (str), email (str), phone (str), created_at (str)
2. Create Invoice dataclass in src/models/invoice.py with fields: id (str), client_id (str), number (str), total_cents (int), status (str), issued_at (str)
3. Use @dataclass(frozen=True) decorator for immutability
4. Use proper type hints with built-in types (str, int) not typing module
5. Add descriptive docstrings for each class
6. Export classes in models/__init__.py for easy importing
tasks.verificationCriteria: Client and Invoice dataclasses can be instantiated with all required fields. Type hints use built-in types only. Classes are frozen (immutable). Can be imported via 'from src.models import Client, Invoice'. Fields match Jobber API schema exactly.
tasks.analysisResult: Phase 1 establishes the foundational object-oriented architecture for TightBeam v2 Jobber data migration tool. The implementation follows exact specifications from shrimp-rules.md and prepares for seamless integration with Phase 2 (JobberClient, EntityMapper), Phase 3 (MigrationCoordinator, CLI), and Phase 4 (testing and refinement). All classes must use constructor-based dependency injection, single responsibility principle, and built-in dict type instead of typing.Dict (UP035 rule compliance).

tasks.name: Implement AuthProvider Class
tasks.description: Create AuthProvider class for reading and validating JOBBER_TOKEN environment variable with proper error handling. This class handles all authentication concerns and provides a clean interface for token access throughout the application.
tasks.notes: This class must be implemented before JobberClient in Phase 2. Must use domain-specific ConfigurationError for missing token scenarios.

relatedFiles.description: ConfigurationError exception used for missing token

tasks.implementationGuide:
1. Create AuthProvider class in src/auth/auth_provider.py
2. Implement constructor with no dependencies (reads environment directly)
3. Implement get_token() method returning string
4. Raise ConfigurationError if JOBBER_TOKEN environment variable is missing
5. Add get_headers() method returning dict with Authorization header
6. Use os.environ to read environment variable
7. Include comprehensive docstrings and type hints
8. Follow single responsibility principle - only handle authentication
tasks.verificationCriteria: AuthProvider can be instantiated without parameters. get_token() returns valid token when JOBBER_TOKEN is set. Raises ConfigurationError when JOBBER_TOKEN is missing. get_headers() returns proper Authorization header format. Class follows single responsibility principle.

tasks.name: Implement Repository with Schema and CRUD Interface
tasks.description: Create Repository class with SQLite schema initialization and generic CRUD operations for Client and Invoice entities. This class abstracts all database operations and provides a clean interface for data persistence following the Repository pattern.
tasks.notes: Database schema must match shrimp-rules.md exactly. All SQL operations must use parameterized queries for security. Repository must be generic to support both entity types.

relatedFiles.description: Repository class with SQLite operations and CRUD interface
Client and Invoice models used in repository operations

tasks.implementationGuide:
1. Create Repository class in src/repositories/repository.py
2. Implement constructor accepting sqlite3.Connection dependency
3. Implement init_schema() method creating clients and invoices tables
4. Use exact SQL schema from shrimp-rules.md with CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS
5. Implement generic CRUD methods: create(), read(), update(), delete()
6. Use parameterized queries for all SQL operations
7. Add save_clients() and save_invoices() batch methods
8. Include proper error handling with RepositoryError
9. Support both Client and Invoice entity types
10. Follow dependency injection pattern
tasks.verificationCriteria: Repository can be instantiated with sqlite3.Connection. init_schema() creates tables matching exact schema from shrimp-rules.md. CRUD operations work for both Client and Invoice entities. All SQL uses parameterized queries. Batch save methods handle List[Client] and List[Invoice]. Proper error handling with RepositoryError.
